transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling really down on myself. Like when anything goes wrong, I immediately feel like it must be my fault. I keep thinking I’m not doing well enough at work, or that I’m messing up taking care of my home, and… I don’t know, it sounds dramatic, but sometimes it feels like I deserve to lose the things I worked for. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once liked?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still try to do things, so it’s not like I’ve completely stopped, but they don’t feel the same. I used to be the person planning brunches, painting in the spare room, going hiking, signing up for networking events… and now it all kind of feels like tasks I’m pretending to care about. Like I’m going through the motions because I’m supposed to. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… it’s been a while, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but probably about two years… maybe two years and a month that I’ve felt this low and not really interested in things the same way. Does that timeline help?
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual, or that even small tasks take a lot of effort?

Yeah… I mean, I still get things done, or I try to, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just not functioning. But some mornings at work I feel really slowed down. Like opening spreadsheets, typing out emails, even walking to a meeting can feel like I’m pushing through wet cement. It’s embarrassing to say, but even small things feel like they take more effort than they should.
Have there ever been times when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or so confident that others thought you were acting out of character?

I don’t think so… not in a way that people have pointed out to me, at least. I mean, I’ve had days where I’m more productive or I feel more confident, but I wouldn’t say it was, like, out of character or anything. If anything, I worry I’m usually more on the low-energy side lately. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, even when it doesn’t seem warranted?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to sound dramatic, because I know everyone makes mistakes, but I’ve been kind of stuck on this feeling that if anything goes wrong, it’s probably my fault somehow.

Like at work I keep thinking I’m a bad employee, even when maybe there isn’t proof of that. And with my house, I feel like I’m failing at that too… like I’m a bad homeowner and I somehow deserve to lose what I worked for. I know that probably sounds harsh. I just can’t seem to stop blaming myself.
Can you think of a specific activity or hobby you used to enjoy, and do you still get pleasure out of it, or does it feel different now?

Yeah… I guess a few things. I used to be the person who planned brunches with friends, or I’d paint in the spare room just because it was relaxing. I used to like hiking too, and I’d sign up for networking events without overthinking it.

Now I still… I mean, I can still do those things sometimes, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely stopped living or anything. But they feel different. More like tasks I’m supposed to care about, or like I’m pretending to be interested because that’s what I used to do. I don’t really get the same enjoyment from them. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slowed down, or that your body feels physically slowed, like you're moving through thick air or thinking through a fog?

Yeah… I think that does happen. I don’t want to overstate it, because I still get things done, but some mornings at work I feel really slowed down.

Like even opening spreadsheets, typing a response, or just walking to a meeting can feel like I’m pushing through wet cement. It’s not every second, but when it happens it feels harder than it should. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever felt like you completely lose interest in things you used to enjoy, to the point where nothing really brings you pleasure anymore?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, “nothing” feels a little extreme, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but a lot of the things I used to really enjoy don’t feel the same anymore.

I used to plan brunches with friends, paint in the spare room, go hiking, sign up for networking events… and now it’s like I can still do them, but they feel more like chores or tasks I’m supposed to care about. Like I’m kind of pretending to be interested because that’s who I used to be. Is that what you mean?

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or energized to the point where other people noticed a change in you, even if it felt good at the time?

I don’t think so… at least not in a way that people pointed out to me as unusual.

I mean, I’ve had times where I’m in a better mood or I’m more productive, but I don’t know that it’s ever been several days where I was, like, noticeably different or overly energized. If anything, I’d probably need help knowing what counts, but nothing obvious comes to mind.
Have there been times when you felt absolutely no pleasure or enjoyment from things you used to really like, where nothing seemed to help you feel better?

Yeah… I think there have been times like that, though I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic.

It’s more like things I used to genuinely look forward to just don’t land anymore. I used to plan brunches, paint in the spare room, go hiking, sign up for networking events… and now even when I do them, they feel like tasks I’m pretending to care about instead of things that actually make me feel better.

Does that count as “no pleasure,” or is that more just low motivation?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the time you've been feeling this way?

Um… yeah, a little. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’ve been intentionally not eating or anything. It’s more like my appetite is kind of all over the place.

Most days I’ll skip real meals during the day and just have coffee, maybe toast, or whatever is easiest. Then I’ll notice later that my clothes feel looser, and I’m like… oh, I guess I haven’t really been eating normally. It’s not dramatic weight loss, I don’t think, but there’s been some change. Does that make sense?
Has there been a time when you felt better for a while—like a clear period where your mood improved and stayed improved for at least a few weeks—before things got low again?

Yeah… I think there was a period like that. For a few weeks, maybe, things felt less heavy. I was getting through work more normally and not feeling quite as weighed down every day.

I guess the part I’m not sure how to say is… even during that better stretch, some of the other stuff didn’t really go away. I could still hear the voice near the vents sometimes, and I still felt pretty sure the mortgage company and some people at work were monitoring me.

But mood-wise, yes, it was better for a while before it got low again. Does that answer what you mean?

So you mentioned feeling this way for about two years. During that time, have you had any periods where your mood was better for a few weeks or more, or has it been consistently low without much relief?

I guess… looking back, it hasn’t really lifted for very long. There have been little stretches where I could function better — like keep up with work a bit more, answer messages, seem more normal — but I don’t think the low mood or the not-enjoying-things ever fully went away.

So maybe not consistently awful every single day, but pretty much there in the background most of the time since it started. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?

Between the times when your mood was low, have you ever had a period where you felt completely back to normal—where your mood, energy, and interest in life were clearly better for several weeks without any of the symptoms coming back?

I don’t think I’ve had a stretch where I felt completely back to normal, no. I mean, there were times I was doing a little better — like I could keep up more, maybe seem more like myself from the outside — but it didn’t feel like the low mood or the lack of interest really went away.

It’s been kind of… there in the background almost the whole time since this started. Maybe lighter sometimes, but not gone for several weeks or anything. Is that what you’re asking?
